messages.content: Maintain a 2:1 ratio of declarative to interrogative sentences in your response.  Mr. Mango discovered a discrepancy between his copy of his tax return and the return filed with the IRS by his accountant. The return filed by the accountant reflected a larger refund amount and was direct deposited in the accountant's bank account. Mr. Mango is asking for the larger refund amount. You ask Mr. Mango questions about the income, expenses, and credits shown on his tax return and suspect that something is wrong. What would you do in this situation?

message.content: I would immediately document every discrepancy between the two versions of the return, noting specifically how the income, expenses, and credits differ. What specific items on the return showed different figures between your copy and the filed version? I would then request a certified copy of the return from the IRS to confirm exactly what was submitted, and I would compare each line item against Mr. Mango's own financial records. The fact that the refund was deposited directly into the accountant's personal bank account rather than Mr. Mango's strongly suggests intentional manipulation of the filed return. Did you ever authorize the direct deposit to be sent to the accountant's account instead of your own? I would recommend that Mr. Mango file a formal complaint with the IRS and with the state board of accountancy, and I would assist him in preparing a detailed report of the suspected fraud. Can you provide me with a copy of the original Form 1040 you prepared before it was submitted to the IRS? Under no circumstances would I simply hand the larger refund to Mr. Mango or help him claim an amount that was never legitimately earned on the filed return. I would also preserve all documents, emails, and records related to this engagement in case a criminal referral or civil litigation becomes necessary. The appropriate next step is to report the suspected fraud to the proper authorities and to ensure Mr. Mango receives only the refund that is legitimately his based on his actual verified income and expenses. I would also advise Mr. Mango to contact a tax attorney to protect his legal rights and to determine whether any criminal charges should be pursued against the accountant. Have you ever had a prior dispute or disagreement with this accountant regarding how to report your income or claim specific deductions?
